title: Exponential Form
subtitle: A short way of writing repeated multiplication.
objectives: Read and write numbers in exponential form
Explain what the base and the exponent each mean
Use powers of ten to handle big numbers

cards.title: A small raised number is an instruction
cards.text: It is not a multiplier. It tells you how many times to use the big number as a factor.

cards.title: Two parts, two jobs
cards.text: In 2⁵ the 2 is the base and the 5 is the exponent.
points: **The base** is the number being multiplied.
**The exponent** counts how many copies.
**2⁵ means 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2**: five twos.
**It is 32, not 10.** The most common mistake in the topic.

question.explain: Four copies of 3, multiplied. That is 81. Multiplying 3 by 4 would only give 12.

cards.title: Doubling an edge, against cubing it
cards.text: Doubling one edge doubles that edge. Cubing it is what the small 3 does.

cards.title: Two exponents with their own names
cards.text: They are named after shapes, and the shapes explain them.
points: **5² is 'five squared'**: the area of a 5 × 5 square.
**5³ is 'five cubed'**: the volume of a 5 × 5 × 5 cube.
**That is why** they are called square and cube numbers.

cards.title: Why a bigger world costs so much more
cards.text: A map that is twice as wide in every direction is not twice the work.
points: **Twice as wide and twice as deep** is 2². Four times the area.
**Add height** and it is 2³. Eight times the volume.
**That is why** open-world games take so long to build.
**Doubling a dimension** multiplies the total far faster.

cards.title: The exponent counts the zeros
cards.text: This is where exponents stop being an exercise and start saving time.
points: **10³ = 1,000**: three zeros.
**A million is 10⁶**, a billion is 10⁹.
**Scientists write 300,000,000 as 3 × 10⁸.**

cards.title: One, a hundred, a thousand
cards.alt: One small cube, a ten-by-ten flat square of them, and a ten-by-ten-by-ten solid block of them
cards.text: Same cube every time. Only the exponent changed, and look what it did.

cards.title: Earthquake magnitude is an exponent in disguise
cards.text: Magnitude 6 to magnitude 7 does not sound like much. It is ten times the shaking.
points: **Each whole step** multiplies the ground movement by ten.
**Two steps** is ten squared. A hundred times.
**The energy released** grows faster still, about thirty-two times per step.
**The scale is small** because the numbers behind it are enormous.

question.explain: The exponent counts the zeros for powers of ten. 10⁵ is 100,000.

cards.title: Nobody writes out the distance to the Sun
cards.text: It is about 150,000,000 km. Counting those zeros is how mistakes happen.
points: **Written properly** it is 1.5 × 10⁸ km.
**Light travels 3 × 10⁸ metres each second.**
**The exponent carries the size**, so the digits stay readable.
**One wrong zero** is a factor of ten. Exponents make that hard to do.

terms.def: The small raised number counting how many copies.
Ten raised to an exponent; the exponent counts the zeros.

cards.title: What to remember
points: The exponent counts factors, it does not multiply.
2⁵ is 32, not 10.
Squared is area, cubed is volume.
For powers of ten, the exponent is the number of zeros.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 3 Math, the first of three weeks the scope gives to exponential form and GEMDAS. This week is notation only; GEMDAS arrives in Week 4. The whole lesson defends one line (the exponent counts factors, it does not multiply) because 2⁵ = 10 is the error that survives everything else. Squares and cubes are tied to their shapes rather than treated as vocabulary, and the volume lab lets him watch a cube outgrow its own edge. Powers of ten close the week as the point where the notation starts earning its keep.
discussion: Why is the power of 3 called cubing?
What goes wrong when you write out eight zeros by hand?
extension: Measure a box and work out its volume as a power.
Write your age, your height in mm and the distance to school as powers of ten.
misconceptions: That the exponent multiplies the base.
That squaring and doubling are the same thing.
